BMAssassin_ASN21Mace.overview: The Assassin was introduced in 2676 as the product of corporate ambition rather than military necessity. Maltex Corporation successfully lobbied the Star League to purchase the design as a replacement for the lighter Wasp and Stinger reconnaissance 'Mechs, achieving this through over-hyped performance statistics, fudged budget approximations, and political maneuvering. Despite this inauspicious origin, the forty-ton Assassin proved itself a capable light 'Mech hunter with impressive speed and jumping capability, and its modular design and ease of maintenance allowed it to persist through centuries of warfare long after Maltex's own fortunes had faded. Hellespont 'Mech Works revived the chassis in the late Jihad era, ensuring the Assassin remains a common sight in Capellan and Periphery forces.
BMAssassin_ASN21Mace.capabilities:
The Assassin combines respectable mobility with adequate firepower for its intended role as a reconnaissance platform and light 'Mech hunter. Its VOX 280 fusion engine propels the forty-ton chassis to speeds of 118 kilometers per hour, while seven Lox Lift Series 1 jump jets provide an impressive 210-meter jumping distance that allows pilots to exploit terrain advantages against heavier opponents.

The weapons suite centers on a Holly-5 LRM-5 launcher for long-range harassment, supplemented by a Holly-2 SRM-2 rack and arm-mounted Martell medium laser for close engagements. This combination provides flexibility across engagement ranges, though the design's limited ammunition capacity of just seventy-four total rounds restricts extended operations without resupply. The SRM launcher's ammunition feed system is also prone to jamming in high-heat situations, a persistent concern that has led many operators to adopt conservative firing disciplines during sustained engagements.

The Assassin's most significant weakness lies in its cockpit design. Maltex's cost-cutting measures produced one of the most cramped cockpits in the Inner Sphere, limiting pilot endurance to half that of comparable designs and causing many veterans to develop chronic back problems. Despite numerous redesign attempts over four centuries, this fundamental flaw has never been adequately addressed in standard production models.
BMAssassin_ASN21Mace.history:
The Assassin's troubled history began when Maltex Corporation secured Star League Defense Force contracts through aggressive lobbying rather than superior design. Only several hundred units were produced before quality control investigations slowed production to a crawl, and the design was quietly shuffled to Periphery garrisons and militia markets. The primary manufacturing facility on Errai was destroyed in 2835 during the Second Succession War, further limiting the chassis's availability.

House Marik became the Assassin's most enthusiastic user during the Third Succession War. The 'Mech's impressive performance during the Battle of Rochelle in 2980, where it excelled in muddy conditions that hampered heavier designs, led to widespread adoption in Free Worlds League garrison forces. Marik commanders frequently assigned Assassins to rear-area raiding parties, where their speed and jump capability proved invaluable for hit-and-run operations.

The Capellan Confederation exhausted its Assassin inventory by 3025, and spare parts shortages plagued operators across the Inner Sphere. By 3058, most surviving Assassins had been phased out of frontline service, with the remaining examples typically serving as family heirlooms passed down through MechWarrior dynasties, often sporting extensive field modifications.

The Assassin's fortunes reversed dramatically in late 3067 when Hellespont 'Mech Works acquired the design from Maltex Corporation. Distracted by Jihad-era chaos, tax evasion charges, and suspected Word of Blake connections, Maltex readily surrendered control. Hellespont began producing upgraded variants for the Capellan Confederation Armed Forces, Taurian Defense Force, and Magistracy Armed Forces, using the chassis as an economical means to rebuild shattered formations. The design's shared components with the Raven II further simplified logistics for Capellan operators.

Defiance Industries' attempt to produce the ASN-30 variant for Lyran forces during the FedCom Civil War proved largely unsuccessful, with the radical redesign failing to win acceptance. However, Hellespont's more conservative upgrades have ensured the Assassin remains a common sight in Capellan and Periphery forces well into the thirty-second century.
BMAssassin_ASN21Mace.deployment: This variant served as the standard production Assassin for nearly four centuries and remains the most widely encountered variant. Originally distributed to Star League Defense Force garrison commands and Periphery postings, the base model found its greatest concentration in Free Worlds League service, where House Marik adopted it enthusiastically for rear-area security and raiding operations. Smaller numbers filtered into Lyran and Davion militia forces through battlefield salvage and gray-market sales. The ASN-21's straightforward maintenance requirements made it a favorite of independent commands and mercenary units operating far from established supply lines, though operators quickly learned to manage the cockpit's ergonomic limitations through shortened patrol rotations and frequent crew swaps.

BMAtlasII_AS7DH2BMUpgraded.overview: Designed in 2755 to maintain the SLDF's edge over the League's Member States, the AS7-D Atlas remains a formidable assault 'Mech even today. But to General Aleksandr Kerensky that was only the beginning, and an advanced version developed for the Royal BattleMech regiments was just beginning deployment on the eve of the bloody Amaris Coup. At one hundred tons, the Atlas II refined its predecessor's already formidable combination of firepower, protection, and psychological impact, incorporating Star League-era technologies to create what many consider the definitive Royal assault 'Mech. Its extreme rarity and storied lineage have made the Atlas II one of the most sought-after chassis in the Inner Sphere and Clan space alike.
BMAtlasII_AS7DH2BMUpgraded.capabilities:
An evolution of the iconic AS7-D, the AS7-D-H Atlas II retains the basic structure and electronics. The original missile armament is retained, but a smaller caliber arm-mounted LB 10-X autocannon replaces the heavy autocannon. Installed in a double mount on the left forearm, extended-range large lasers complement the autocannon and LRM launcher. With this heavier arm-mounted weaponry, rear-firing weaponry was deemed redundant and the medium lasers (upgraded to pulse models) were switched to fire forward.

There was no way to surpass the Atlas' legendary armor, but upgrading to ferro-fibrous allowed CASE to be installed. Many of the stylistic alterations in the BattleMech's appearance were made during this change in armor type.

The trade-offs in this redesign are notable. The LB 10-X, while versatile with its cluster and slug ammunition options, lacks the devastating close-range stopping power of the original AC/20 that made the standard Atlas such a fearsome brawler. Additionally, the Atlas II's extreme rarity has always posed significant logistics challenges. Spare parts, particularly for the advanced ferro-fibrous armor and LB 10-X feed system, are difficult to source outside of major manufacturing centers, and field repairs often require cannibalization of other advanced 'Mechs.
BMAtlasII_AS7DH2BMUpgraded.notes: Bubbles' Marauders Atlas II updated for IlClan era.
BMAtlasII_AS7DH2BMUpgraded.history:
The Atlas II was still in its first stages of deployment when the New Vandenburg Revolt sparked off the Periphery uprisings in 2765. Facing formidable odds, these few AS7-D-Hs performed magnificently in the hands of their Royal regiment pilots. General Kerensky himself piloted one during his escape from New Vandenburg, evidence of the faith the Commanding General placed in his enhanced Atlas design.

With the news that the Terran Hegemony had fallen under Amaris' control, Kerensky led his troops to secure the lightly defended Rim Worlds Republic as a base of operations. Captured Republican factories were repurposed to produce Atlas IIs for Royal commands as they fought the grueling campaign to liberate the Terran Hegemony. When the time came for the Exodus, the Atlas II's fate diverged sharply from its predecessor. While many standard AS7-D Atlas pilots chose to remain in the Inner Sphere, the surviving Atlas II pilots chose almost unanimously to follow their Commanding General into exile. The Atlas II thus vanished from the Inner Sphere entirely, becoming a near-mythical machine known only from old records and fading memories.

In the Clan Homeworlds, the Atlas II became one of the most prized assault 'Mechs. The Clans treasured every example discovered in Brian Caches during their formative years. The most famous Atlas II in Clan history was piloted by ilKhan Nicholas Kerensky himself, eldest son of Aleksandr. Nicholas had followed his father into exile and, after the elder Kerensky's death, forged the scattered exiles into twenty Clans. He led them on a crusade to retake the war-ravaged Pentagon worlds in 2821. Thirteen years later, in 2834, ilKhan Nicholas Kerensky died at the controls of his Atlas II when he intervened in a Trial of Grievance between Widowmaker Khan Cal Jorgensson and Wolf Khan Jerome Winson. The Widowmakers had committed a gross breach of zellbrigen, and when Kerensky stepped between the combatants, Khan Jorgensson fired into the Atlas II's cockpit, killing the ilKhan and sealing Clan Widowmaker's fate. The destruction of the Widowmakers that followed remains one of the most consequential events in Clan history.

The Atlas II returned to the Inner Sphere in dramatic fashion. A single example was sighted among the Jade Falcon Touman during the fighting on Tukayyid in 3052, sending shockwaves through ComStar intelligence analysts who had believed the design extinct. During the Jihad, when the Word of Blake captured Defiance Industries' factories on Hesperus II, they produced several runs of the Atlas II for their forces. The enigmatic Devlin Stone piloted one such machine, the "Phantom," in its distinctive black-and-white skeletal color scheme, as he led his growing coalition against the Blakists. Stone personally commanded from the Atlas II's cockpit during the Trial of Possession against a Star of Ghost Bears on Tukayyid in 3073, and led the flanking maneuver that shattered the Blakist Third Division on Skye in 3074. After the coalition forces evicted the Word of Blake from Hesperus II, Defiance Industries chose to keep the Atlas II in production, finally returning this legendary Royal 'Mech to the Inner Sphere after nearly three centuries of absence.
BMAtlasII_AS7DH2BMUpgraded.deployment: Produced in very limited numbers before the fall of the First Star League, this variant was a more aggressive long-range variant of the Atlas II. Both ER large lasers were replaced with a Kinslaughter ER PPC, and a Gauss rifle took the place of the LB 10-X autocannon, concentrating the design's firepower into fewer but more powerful weapons. One heat sink was removed to accommodate the weight changes. The resulting 'Mech delivered devastating alpha strikes at extreme range, though the reduced number of weapons left it more vulnerable if individual systems were damaged. With the destruction of the New Earth production facility in 2767 during the Amaris Coup, no further examples were produced, making the H2 one of the rarest Atlas variants in existence.
BMAtlasII_AS7DH2BMUpgraded.manufacturer: Hegemony Research and Development Department, Weapons Division

BMAtlas_AS7D.overview: First deployed in 2755, the Atlas was commissioned by General Aleksandr Kerensky as the ultimate expression of assault 'Mech doctrine. He demanded "a 'Mech as powerful as imaginable, as impenetrable as possible, and as foreboding as conceivable, so that fear itself will be our ally." Built by the Hegemony's premier manufacturers, the hundred-ton Atlas was intended to give the Regular Army a decisive advantage over the growing House Lord armies. Despite the upheaval that followed and the abandonment of the Inner Sphere by General Kerensky and most of the SLDF, the Atlas served its purpose and has endured as the most recognized and feared assault 'Mech in existence.
BMAtlas_AS7D.capabilities:
The first impression any spectator gets of the Atlas is its ferocious appearance. Although there are taller 'Mechs on the field, none of them have the sheer presence of the Atlas.

As an assault 'Mech, the Atlas has few peers. The largest long-range missile launcher available sits in the left torso, giving the Atlas a powerful long-range punch. BMAtlas_AS7D.history:
The Atlas was born of necessity. Between 2751 and 2761, the Cameron Edicts passed by the High Council permitted the five House Lords to double the size of their personal armies. The Regular Army needed a weapon that could maintain its supremacy over these swelling forces. General Aleksandr Kerensky himself laid down the specifications, demanding "a 'Mech as powerful as possible, as impenetrable as possible, and as ugly and foreboding as conceivable, so that fear itself will be our ally." Designers took this mandate to heart, spending an entire year perfecting the skull-shaped head that would earn the Atlas its enduring nickname: the "Death's Head."

The Atlas saw its baptism of fire against Stefan the Usurper during the liberation of Terra. In the final battles to secure Earth's major spaceports, the Atlas was instrumental in establishing beachheads that allowed SLDF troops to land safely. General Kerensky's second-in-command, General Aaron DeChavilier, directed the assault on the Usurper's last stronghold, the Imperial City. DeChavilier continually exposed his Atlas to enemy fire, marching forward as if laser bolts, missiles, and cannon shells were nothing more than the annoying buzz of flies. When DeChavilier's Atlas pushed over the concrete outer wall surrounding the Imperial Palace, Kerensky headed for the gates in his Orion. It was a scene that would be immortalized in countless holovids and paintings, forever linking the Atlas to the liberation of humanity's homeworld.

When Kerensky departed on his Exodus, he wanted all Atlases to accompany him. More than two-thirds of Atlas pilots, however, refused to join, perhaps believing they could better their fortunes by remaining in the Inner Sphere. The remaining Atlases and those still rolling off assembly lines on Hesperus II, Al Na'ir, and Quentin continued to inspire terror wherever they walked. As the Succession Wars ravaged the Inner Sphere, the Atlas spread to every major military in limited numbers. Most militaries were loath to tamper with the design for the simple reason that it seemed nearly perfect in its role already, and attempted modifications generally failed since engineers had to make too many concessions to keep the 'Mech functioning.

The Atlas cemented its legend during some of the most key moments in Inner Sphere history. On Mallory's World in 3013, First Prince Ian Davion of the Federated Suns held a vital pass against Yorinaga Kurita and the Second Sword of Light while his men made their escape. Although the Kell Hounds and other units pushed forward to support him, Prince Davion fell in battle before help could arrive. A warrior first and a leader second, his sacrifice from the cockpit of an Atlas became one of the most celebrated last stands in military history. Two decades later, the sight of Hanse Davion's Atlases and Victors standing in formation for honors after actions against House Kurita reminded the Inner Sphere that the 'Mech remained the gold standard of assault warfare.

The technological renaissance of the 3040s and 3050s breathed new life into the venerable design. The Draconis Combine debuted the AS7-K variant, transforming the Atlas from a short-ranged brawler into a long-range bombardier. Improved ballistic and energy weapons replaced the original close-quarters armament, extending the 'Mech's reach considerably. Despite being an ancient design, the Atlas' reputation on the battlefield remained unquestioned, and even state-of-the-art machines gave it a wide berth. This was, after all, the flagship of all BattleMechs, and there was still no projected date for it to be replaced.

The Jihad tested the Atlas as never before. On Al Na'ir in early 3069, a lance of corporate-owned Atlases held off wave after wave of Word of Blake troops while defending a dome settlement for several days, eventually succumbing only when penetrating torso hits crippled their powerplants. The Word of Blake's capture of Hesperus II in 3070 temporarily halted Defiance Industries' production lines, a crisis that spurred development of new Atlas variants at secondary facilities. When Hesperus was finally liberated, these newer models entered full production alongside the original.

Through all of this, the Atlas has transcended its role as a mere weapon of war to become a cultural icon. It appears on more recruiting posters, more propaganda films, and in the boxes of more children's toys than any other BattleMech. More than a dozen variants have appeared over the centuries, each one building on a legacy that stretches back to the final days of the Star League. Whether defending a beleaguered colony or leading an assault on a fortified position, the sight of the Death's Head advancing across the battlefield continues to inspire allies and strike fear into enemies, just as General Kerensky intended nearly three centuries ago.
BMAtlas_AS7D.deployment: As the original production model, this variant has been the backbone of Atlas deployments since its introduction. Nearly every Atlas built during the Star League era remained in the Inner Sphere when Kerensky departed, and production continued at Hesperus II, Al Na'ir, and Quentin to supply the Successor States. The design spread in limited numbers to every major military, where it served most often as a command vehicle for senior officers or as the anchor of heavy and assault lances. Most militaries were loath to tamper with the design for the simple reason that it seemed nearly perfect in its role already, and the D model continues to be fielded by front-line and militia units across the Inner Sphere centuries after its introduction.

BMAwesome_AWS8Q.overview: Introduced in 2665 by the Technicron Manufacturing Conglomerate for the Star League Defense Force, the Awesome was designed as a replacement for the aging STR-2C Striker. An eighty-ton assault 'Mech built around a punishing PPC-based armament, the Awesome earned a fearsome reputation as a durable fire-support platform capable of anchoring any battle line. Its near-total independence from ammunition resupply and notoriously difficult-to-kill design have made it one of the most valued assault 'Mechs among logistics officers and field commanders alike. Sought after by every Great House and mercenary command with the means to acquire one, the design has remained a mainstay of assault lances for over four centuries.
BMAwesome_AWS8Q.capabilities:
The standard AWS-8Q carries three Kreuss PPCs as its primary armament: one mounted in the right arm and two split between the left and right torsos. This battery delivers devastating firepower at ranges exceeding five hundred meters, enough to cripple most targets with a single concentrated volley. A Diverse Optics Type 10 Small Laser mounted in the head provides a token close-range weapon, while the left arm terminates in a battlefist for hand-to-hand engagements. A Pitban 240 fusion engine gives the Awesome a top speed of 64.8 kilometers per hour, adequate for an assault 'Mech but insufficient to dictate engagement range against faster opponents.

Twenty-eight standard heat sinks give the Awesome remarkable staying power in prolonged engagements, allowing MechWarriors to maintain a steady two-three-two firing cycle without significant heat buildup. The design carries fifteen tons of standard armor, exceeding even the BattleMaster in total protection, and the placement of critical systems away from explosive components makes the Awesome notoriously difficult to achieve a kill against. Rear armor coverage is among the heaviest found on any assault 'Mech, frustrating attempts by flanking units to exploit the typical weak point.

The Awesome is not without significant drawbacks, however. Its PPCs suffer from the minimum range limitations inherent to the weapon type, making close-quarters combat a serious vulnerability. With only the small laser and a single fist to fall back on at short range, the design is poorly equipped to handle opponents that close inside its effective engagement envelope. The lack of any weapon mount on the left arm further limits its options. The 'Mech's modest ground speed leaves it vulnerable to flanking maneuvers by faster opponents seeking to bypass the forward PPC arc, and commanders who fail to account for these limitations often find their Awesomes isolated and overwhelmed.
BMAwesome_AWS8Q.history:
Technicron Manufacturing developed the Awesome on Savannah in the Free Worlds League, delivering the first production units to the SLDF in 2665 as a direct replacement for the aging Striker. The design proved itself quickly, and by the time of the Amaris Coup the Awesome had secured a place in front-line regiments across the Star League. When the SLDF departed on the Exodus, significant numbers of Awesomes remained behind with the Successor State militaries, setting the stage for the design's long career in the wars to come.

The Succession Wars placed enormous strain on Awesome production. Technicron's factory complex on Savannah survived the early conflicts largely intact, making it the sole remaining source of new Awesomes by the end of the Second Succession War. This gave the Free Worlds League a decisive advantage in fielding the design, and League diplomats occasionally leveraged Awesome sales as a bargaining tool with other Houses. The loss of advanced manufacturing knowledge during the wars had little effect on the base AWS-8Q, whose reliance on standard components and lack of advanced technology made it one of the easier assault 'Mechs to maintain and produce. Field technicians valued the design for its repairability, and many Awesomes accumulated centuries of continuous service through careful maintenance and component swaps.

The recovery of Star League technology in the 3040s opened new possibilities for the Awesome chassis. Technicron introduced the AWS-9M in 3049, incorporating an XL engine, double heat sinks, and ER PPCs to bring the venerable design into the modern era. The Clan Invasion further accelerated development, and the following decades saw a steady stream of new variants incorporating increasingly advanced technology. Irian BattleMechs Unlimited eventually partnered with other manufacturers on several later models, broadening the Awesome's production base beyond Savannah for the first time in centuries. Through the Jihad and the Dark Age, the Awesome continued to evolve, with Technicron's Savannah facility remaining the primary production center even as new factories on other worlds began contributing their own specialized variants.
BMAwesome_AWS8Q.deployment:
This variant is the standard production model and the most widely encountered variant across the Inner Sphere. Originally fielded by Star League Defense Force line regiments, the base Awesome saw service in every major theater of the Reunification War's aftermath and the early Succession Wars. Its straightforward all-energy loadout made it a natural choice for garrison commands and defensive formations where ammunition resupply was uncertain. SLDF units frequently deployed Awesomes in pairs or lances to create overlapping fields of PPC fire, a tactic adopted by the Successor States and still employed by assault formations to this day.

The Free Worlds League maintained the highest concentration of AWS-8Qs due to its control of the Savannah production lines, and League commanders came to treat the design as the backbone of their heavy assault formations. Other Houses acquired their Awesomes through battlefield salvage, trade, and the occasional raid on League supply depots, ensuring that the 8Q could be found in virtually every major military force across the Inner Sphere.

BMBlackHawk_Sparkles.overview: The Nova, designated Black Hawk by Inner Sphere forces, was among the earliest OmniMechs ever produced when it first rolled off the assembly lines at Tokasha MechWorks in 2870. Designed by Clan Hell's Horses as an infantry support platform, the Nova holds the distinction of being the first OmniMech specifically engineered with connection points allowing Elemental battle armor to mount and dismount the chassis with ease, a feature that would become standard across all subsequent Clan OmniMech designs. Produced by a limited number of facilities over its long service life, the Nova has nonetheless spread to every Clan through trials and salvage, earning a reputation as one of the most versatile and recognizable medium OmniMechs in the Kerensky Cluster and beyond.
BMBlackHawk_Sparkles.capabilities:
The Nova is built around a 250 XL Model SF-2 extralight engine that propels the fifty-ton chassis to a top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour. Five jump jets provide exceptional maneuverability with a jumping distance of one hundred and fifty meters, allowing the Nova to exploit terrain that would stymie heavier opponents. The design carries ten tons of Forge Type HH30 armor, providing ninety-six percent of maximum protection for its weight class, a generous allocation that reflects the Hell's Horses' emphasis on survivability in combined-arms operations.

The chassis dedicates sixteen tons to pod space, enabling a wide range of configurations. In its Primary configuration, the Nova mounts twelve extended-range medium lasers distributed across both arms, creating a devastating close-range barrage capable of shredding battle armor and light vehicles in seconds. However, this firepower comes at a steep cost in waste heat. Even with eighteen double heat sinks, the Nova Prime generates nearly twice as much heat as it can dissipate during a full alpha strike, forcing MechWarriors to carefully manage their fire discipline or risk emergency shutdowns.

The weaknesses of the Nova's design become apparent across its various configurations. The limited pod tonnage constrains heavier weapon loads, and configurations mounting ballistic weapons like the B and C variants often sacrifice secondary armament. However, the combination of speed, jump capability, and configuration flexibility has made the Nova one of the most versatile medium OmniMechs ever fielded.
BMBlackHawk_Sparkles.history:
The Nova made its battlefield debut in 2872 during the combined assault on Kindraa Smythe-Jewel on Foster, launched by the Hell's Horses alongside Clan Coyote and Kindraa Payne. The attack proved devastatingly effective, wiping out the Smythe-Jewels as a faction and establishing the Nova as a proven combat design. The Hell's Horses' new mechanized battle armor tactics, enabled by the Nova's Elemental mounting points, proved so successful that the concept became standard on all subsequent OmniMechs.

Originally manufactured at a single facility on Tokasha, production ceased in 2921 when Clan Ghost Bear captured the world during the Battle of Tokasha, after which the facility produced only spare parts. Every Clan acquired examples through trials and salvage over the following centuries, ensuring the design remained ubiquitous if increasingly scarce. The Nova's versatility as a jack of all trades saw it deployed across every major Clan conflict of the Golden Century and beyond, though it was increasingly relegated to a secondary role as heavier and lighter OmniMechs entered service.

The Clan Invasion of the Inner Sphere in 3049 brought the Nova to the attention of the Great Houses, where it earned the reporting name Black Hawk. Inner Sphere encounters with the design directly inspired the Draconis Combine's Black Hawk-KU program and later the Penetrator developed by Kallon Industries. The Nova's balanced design proved so influential that it spawned an entire lineage of derivative designs across both Clan and Inner Sphere production lines.

Clan Jade Falcon resurrected Nova production at Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten in 3073, over two hundred years after the original lines fell silent, breathing new life into the aging design. The Falcons fielded Novas extensively during their campaigns in the mid-thirty-second century, including the invasion of Arc-Royal in 3146, where a Star of Novas from the Fifty-Third Falcon Talon intercepted elements of the First Wolf Legion Cluster screening the evacuation of the Exiled Wolf leadership. The Novas' varied configurations caused confusion among the defenders, enabling the Falcon Trinary to press their advantage.

Meanwhile, Clan Hell's Horses maintained a particularly large concentration of Novas in their touman, and in the mid-3140s numerous examples found their way into the Hell's Horses forces during the Golden Ordun alliance. The last Nova production facility in the Clan Homeworlds, on Sheridan under Clan Star Adder control, was eventually retooled to produce Pouncers by 3087, leaving the few remaining Homeworld examples in the hands of Aggressor MechWarriors operating on the fringes of Clan society.
BMBlackHawk_Sparkles.deployment: The Primary configuration epitomizes the Nova's close-combat philosophy, mounting twelve extended-range medium lasers split evenly across both arms. Four additional double heat sinks supplement the chassis's base fourteen, though even eighteen sinks cannot fully manage the tremendous heat output of a full alpha strike. This configuration excels as a battle armor killer and close-range brawler, but demands exceptional heat management discipline from its MechWarrior to avoid potentially catastrophic shutdowns in sustained engagements.

BMBlackKnight_BL6BKNTUpgraded.overview:
The Black Knight was introduced in 2578 by Kong Interstellar Corporation as both a front-line combatant and a company- and battalion-level command BattleMech for the Star League Defense Force. Equipped with an advanced communications suite capable of coordinating an entire company of 'Mechs, linking command frequencies across a regiment, and connecting with orbital support satellites, the Black Knight quickly established itself as one of the premier heavy BattleMechs of the Star League era. Built with heavy armor and an all-energy weapons array, the design earned a fearsome reputation that endured across centuries of warfare.

Though the Succession Wars drastically reduced the Black Knight's numbers, the design survived through ComStar stockpiles, field modifications, and the determination of its operators. Production eventually resumed in the 3060s through Robinson Standard BattleWorks and Kong Interstellar's rebuilt facilities, and a succession of increasingly advanced variants has kept the Black Knight relevant on the modern battlefield.
BMBlackKnight_BL6BKNTUpgraded.capabilities:
The Black Knight is an all-energy-weapon platform anchored by a Magna Hellstar II PPC, supported by two large lasers, four medium lasers, and a small laser integrated directly into its Beagle Active Probe. This sensor-weapon linkage allows the scanner to piggyback low-power laser pulses through interfering objects, providing detailed analysis of nearby targets that few other designs can match. Thirteen tons of Valiant Lamellor armor on a Technicron endo steel frame delivers exceptional survivability for a seventy-five-ton chassis, while the standard Vlar 300 engine provides a reliable top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour without the fragility of an extralight powerplant.

The design's primary weakness has always been heat management. Despite mounting twenty single heat sinks, the sheer volume of energy weapons generates heat faster than the cooling system can dissipate it during sustained engagements. MechWarriors must exercise strict fire discipline, selecting weapon groups appropriate to the engagement range rather than attempting full alpha strikes. The original Black Knight's reputation in the Third Heavy Assault Regiment was that of a 'Mech which had to be literally dismembered to stop, and in one-on-one engagements between equally skilled pilots, conventional wisdom holds that the Black Knight will always triumph.
BMBlackKnight_BL6BKNTUpgraded.notes: Bubbles' Marauders Black Knight updated for IlClan era.
BMBlackKnight_BL6BKNTUpgraded.history:
The Black Knight debuted during the Reunification War in 2578 when Kong Interstellar Corporation's Third Heavy Assault Regiment (the Pythons) fielded the new design against the Taurian Concordat on Ridgebrook. Company commanders quickly discovered that the sophisticated electronics package made the Black Knight an outstanding command platform, and following its successful combat debut, the SLDF's First Corps and eventually the entire Defense Force adopted the design. By the height of the Star League, the Black Knight was a ubiquitous presence in SLDF formations, with Royal regiments fielding the advanced BL-6b-KNT variant equipped with double heat sinks and upgraded weaponry.

The collapse of the Star League and the devastation of the First Succession War proved catastrophic for Black Knight production. Kong Interstellar's orbital factories above Connaught were destroyed in 2802, and while the company managed to restart production in 2809 with the downgraded BL-7-KNT (replacing the endo steel chassis and advanced electronics with cruder but manufacturable alternatives) a Capellan Confederation raid permanently destroyed the line in 2820. Kong was reduced to producing spare parts and performing maintenance work, and the Black Knight's numbers slowly dwindled across the Inner Sphere as attrition and jury-rigged repairs took their toll.

During the Succession Wars, the remaining Black Knights were concentrated primarily in the Federated Suns and Free Worlds League, while the Capellan Confederation possessed none. ComStar maintained stockpiles of Star League-era machines, which proved invaluable when the Com Guards adopted the Black Knight as a command unit for Level II and Level III formations. Curiously, the handful of Black Knights provided to the Draconis Combine through Operation ROSEBUD was apparently the result of a clerical error. The Clans also maintained the design, though by the time of the Clan Invasion it had been relegated to solahma units.

The Battle of Tukayyid in 3052 marked the Black Knight's dramatic return to prominence. ComStar engineers developed the BL-9-KNT Clanbuster refit specifically for the engagement, equipping it with an XL engine, upgraded weapons, and a distinctive sword-like hatchet designed to exploit the Clans' disdain for physical combat. These machines proved remarkably effective in the close-quarters fighting of the Racice River Delta against Clan Smoke Jaguar and at Devil's Bath against the Steel Vipers, where the improved short-range firepower and melee capability caught Clan warriors off guard.

Robinson Standard BattleWorks secured a manufacturing license from Kong Interstellar in 3063, producing the technologically advanced BL-12-KNT with extended-range weapons and a targeting computer. Two years later, Kong itself rebuilt its Connaught plant and resumed Black Knight production. Through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, RSB released a succession of increasingly sophisticated BLK-NT variants incorporating Clan-specification weaponry, endo-composite structures, and advanced electronic warfare suites. When the Republic of the Sphere collapsed, Kong received the BLK-NT plans through a reciprocal licensing agreement with RSB and developed its own variant, the BL-18-KNT, updating the classic design with Clan weapons and a targeting computer. The Black Knight has thus endured across nearly six centuries of continuous service, evidence of the fundamental soundness of Kong Interstellar's original design.
BMBlackKnight_BL6BKNTUpgraded.deployment: Reserved for SLDF Royal BattleMech regiments, this variant was introduced in 2751 as a significant upgrade to the base model. The heat dissipation system was overhauled with sixteen double heat sinks, dramatically improving the design's ability to sustain fire. The tonnage savings allowed Kong's engineers to upgrade the large lasers to Raker-X large pulse lasers and replace the standard PPC with a Kinslaughter extended-range model, substantially increasing the Black Knight's effective engagement envelope while maintaining its signature all-energy weapons philosophy.

By the height of the Star League, the Black Knight was a ubiquitous presence in SLDF formations, with Royal regiments fielding the advanced BL-6b-KNT variant equipped with double heat sinks and upgraded weaponry.

The collapse of the Star League and the devastation of the First Succession War proved catastrophic for Black Knight production. Kong Interstellar's orbital factories above Connaught were destroyed in 2802, and while the company managed to restart production in 2809 with the downgraded BL-7-KNT (replacing the endo steel chassis and advanced electronics with cruder but manufacturable alternatives) a Capellan Confederation raid permanently destroyed the line in 2820. Kong was reduced to producing spare parts and performing maintenance work, and the Black Knight's numbers slowly dwindled across the Inner Sphere as attrition and jury-rigged repairs took their toll.

During the Succession Wars, the remaining Black Knights were concentrated primarily in the Federated Suns and Free Worlds League, while the Capellan Confederation possessed none. ComStar maintained stockpiles of Star League-era machines, which proved invaluable when the Com Guards adopted the Black Knight as a command unit for Level II and Level III formations. Curiously, the handful of Black Knights provided to the Draconis Combine through Operation ROSEBUD was apparently the result of a clerical error. The Clans also maintained the design, though by the time of the Clan Invasion it had been relegated to solahma units.

The Battle of Tukayyid in 3052 marked the Black Knight's dramatic return to prominence. ComStar engineers developed the BL-9-KNT Clanbuster refit specifically for the engagement, equipping it with an XL engine, upgraded weapons, and a distinctive sword-like hatchet designed to exploit the Clans' disdain for physical combat. These machines proved remarkably effective in the close-quarters fighting of the Racice River Delta against Clan Smoke Jaguar and at Devil's Bath against the Steel Vipers, where the improved short-range firepower and melee capability caught Clan warriors off guard.

Robinson Standard BattleWorks secured a manufacturing license from Kong Interstellar in 3063, producing the technologically advanced BL-12-KNT with extended-range weapons and a targeting computer. Two years later, Kong itself rebuilt its Connaught plant and resumed Black Knight production. Through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, RSB released a succession of increasingly sophisticated BLK-NT variants incorporating Clan-specification weaponry, endo-composite structures, and advanced electronic warfare suites. When the Republic of the Sphere collapsed, Kong received the BLK-NT plans through a reciprocal licensing agreement with RSB and developed its own variant, the BL-18-KNT, updating the classic design with Clan weapons and a targeting computer. The Black Knight has thus endured across nearly six centuries of continuous service, evidence of the fundamental soundness of Kong Interstellar's original design.
BMBlackKnight_BL6bKNTGorgon.deployment: Reserved for SLDF Royal BattleMech regiments, this variant was introduced in 2751 as a significant upgrade to the base model. The heat dissipation system was overhauled with sixteen double heat sinks, dramatically improving the design's ability to sustain fire. The tonnage savings allowed Kong's engineers to upgrade the large lasers to Raker-X large pulse lasers and replace the standard PPC with a Kinslaughter extended-range model, substantially increasing the Black Knight's effective engagement envelope while maintaining its signature all-energy weapons philosophy.

BMBushwacker_BSWX1Upgraded.overview:
The Bushwacker is a fifty-five-ton medium BattleMech developed by TharHes Industries on Tharkad. Its designers pursued an ambitious goal: a 'Mech with a low-slung, narrow torso intended to present a minimal target profile. While the prototype's speed and firepower impressed evaluators, the cramped internal layout generated chronic electronic interference between the fusion engine and sensor systems that defied every attempted solution. The design appeared destined for cancellation until captured Clan technical data provided the breakthrough needed to resolve these problems.

Full-scale production began in 3053 following the Truce of Tukayyid, and the Bushwacker quickly established itself as a reliable long-range combat platform. Its distinctive narrow profile remains one of its most recognizable and tactically valuable features, and the design has been exported widely across the Inner Sphere.
BMBushwacker_BSWX1Upgraded.capabilities:
The Bushwacker is first and foremost a long-range combat platform. Twin Federated 5-Shot LRM launchers provide indirect fire capability and the ability to deploy specialized munitions including minefields, while a BlazeFire Sweetshot ER large laser and Mydron Model B autocannon deliver punishing direct fire at extended ranges. A pair of Johnston MiniGuns mounted forward offer limited defense against infantry anti-'Mech teams, though they serve as the design's only close-range armament. This weapons configuration encourages pilots to maintain standoff distance, leveraging the Bushwacker's respectable top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour to dictate engagement range.

Nine tons of Kallon Unity Weave ferro-fibrous armor with CASE provides adequate protection for sustained ranged engagements, though it falls short of what many medium 'Mech designs carry. The inclusion of CASE mitigates the risk of ammunition explosion, a meaningful consideration given the Hermes 275 XL engine's vulnerability to side torso damage. Standard tactical doctrine pairs three Bushwackers with a fast light 'Mech acting as a spotter, using cooperative tactics and terrain to maintain effective range while the lance's combined LRM fire wears down approaching enemies. The Bushwacker's distinctive narrow profile, a legacy of its troubled development history, remains one of its most valuable defensive assets on the battlefield.
BMBushwacker_BSWX1Upgraded.notes: Bubbles' Marauders Bushwacker updated for IlClan era.
BMBushwacker_BSWX1Upgraded.history:
The Bushwacker's origins trace to a pre-Clan Invasion development program at TharHes Industries that sought to break with conventional BattleMech design philosophy. The resulting prototype featured a revolutionary low-slung torso but suffered crippling electronic interference between its fusion engine and sensor systems. It was only after the Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth captured Clan technical data during a raid on Twycross that TharHes engineers found their solution, adapting internal layout techniques from captured Vulture schematics to resolve the interference problems.

Full production began on Tharkad in 3053, though preproduction models had already reached FedCom units serving on the Clan frontlines during the initial invasion. This early distribution meant the Bushwacker was initially most numerous along the Clan border and within Lyran Alliance commands following the secession of the Federated Commonwealth. By the conclusion of the FedCom Civil War, however, the design had spread to nearly every first echelon unit in both successor states. The Bushwacker became an inexplicable favorite among MechWarriors serving in the Draconis and Capellan Marches of the Federated Suns, far from its Lyran origins.

The Jihad proved a turning point for the design's manufacturing history. Word of Blake forces occupied Tharkad and badly damaged TharHes Industries' production facilities. Desperate for capital to rebuild, TharHes sold the Bushwacker's plans to Coventry Metal Works, which used them as the foundation for the Gauntlet OmniMech. Rather than ending the Bushwacker's production run, this arrangement proved mutually beneficial: modern Bushwacker models share a similar frame and various components with the Gauntlet, allowing both manufacturers to reduce costs through economies of scale.

The Bushwacker also served as the basis for the Barghest, a seventy-ton quad BattleMech developed by TharHes at the direction of Archon Katrina Steiner-Davion. TharHes modified the Bushwacker's chassis by repositioning the legs forward and adding a second pair to the rear, increasing overall mass by fifteen tons. Unlike the Gauntlet, the Bushwacker is not restricted to Lyran service and continues to be exported throughout the Inner Sphere, maintaining a strong presence within the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns well into the Dark Age.
BMBushwacker_BSWX1Upgraded.deployment: The original production model fields a balanced long-range armament centered on twin Federated 5-Shot LRM launchers, a BlazeFire Sweetshot ER large laser, and a Mydron Model B autocannon. Two Johnston MiniGuns provide minimal close-range defense. Many FedCom units received preproduction BSW-X1s during the initial Clan Invasion, and the variant remains widespread throughout the Inner Sphere as the most commonly encountered Bushwacker configuration.

BMCatapult_CPLTC1.overview:
The Catapult is a 65-ton fire-support BattleMech first manufactured in 2561 by Hollis Incorporated, a Terran Hegemony defense firm. Designed in anticipation of the Reunification War, the Catapult filled the role of a second-line missile platform capable of punishing enemies at extreme range while maintaining enough mobility to reposition across broken terrain. Hollis produced the chassis in substantial numbers during its initial contract, though the Hegemony deemed the design adequate rather than exceptional and declined to renew the agreement.

Produced across multiple manufacturing runs spanning the late Age of War through the Succession Wars era, the Catapult has remained one of the Inner Sphere's most recognizable heavy BattleMech silhouettes. Its distinctive pod-mounted launchers and armless profile have made it an enduring symbol of indirect fire doctrine, and the chassis has proven remarkably adaptable to a wide range of combat roles well beyond its original missile-support mission.
BMCatapult_CPLTC1.capabilities:
The Catapult is primarily a fire-support platform built around a pair of Holly Long Range Missile 15-rack launchers mounted in distinctive pod-like housings flanking the cockpit. These thirty-tube launchers can begin engaging targets at ranges exceeding 600 meters, well before most opponents can effectively respond. When enemies close within the missiles' minimum effective range, four Martell medium lasers mounted below the cockpit provide adequate short-range defense capable of discouraging most light and medium 'Mechs from pressing an engagement. The design's greatest vulnerability lies in its ammunition dependency, carrying only eight reloads per launcher, which makes the Catapult heavily reliant on logistical support during extended operations.

Ten tons of Durallex Heavy armor provides respectable protection for a fire-support platform, while the Magna 260 fusion engine drives the chassis to a maximum speed of 64 kilometers per hour. Four jump jets grant a 120-meter jumping capability that allows the Catapult to keep pace with faster units across broken terrain. Early production jump jets proved prone to breakdowns that vented heat directly into the 'Mech's interior, a flaw that was addressed in later models but never fully eliminated from all operational units. The lack of arms limits close-quarters capability and leaves the design without anti-infantry weapons, reinforcing the need to maintain standoff distance whenever possible. A distinctive sideways ejection system, while generally considered safe, has been known to surprise pilots unfamiliar with the design.
BMCatapult_CPLTC1.history:
The Catapult's operational history spans centuries of continuous service across the Inner Sphere. Hollis Incorporated was originally a Terran Hegemony company whose first production run of the Catapult predated the colonization of Corey and the formation of the Star League by nearly a decade. During the Star League era, the design served primarily with second-line and specialist formations, including mountaineering regiments that exploited its jump capability in difficult terrain. When Hollis' primary factory transitioned to BattleMaster production, limited spare parts availability caused operational numbers to gradually decline despite continued manufacturing runs that introduced various stylistic changes to the chassis profile.

The fall of the Star League marked a turning point for the Catapult. Many operational units accompanied Aleksandr Kerensky on his Exodus, while the Capellan Confederation secured the largest concentration of those remaining in the Inner Sphere. Hollis' factory on Corey briefly resumed production of new frames and spare parts, and the Draconis Combine simultaneously seized a substantial force during their capture of Dieron. The destruction of the Corey facility at the onset of the First Succession War ended renewed production and ensured the Catapult's increasing rarity throughout that devastating conflict. The design became so prized that entire invasions were launched to capture surviving examples, particularly Federated Suns campaigns against the Capellan Confederation.

The Catapult's scarcity began to reverse in 3033 when Yori 'Mech Works was contracted by the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery to restart production on Al Na'ir, initially focusing on the CPLT-K2 variant. This renewed manufacturing capability paved the way for the CPLT-C3, the first BattleMech to mount the newly rediscovered Arrow IV artillery system. Despite a rushed development cycle that reintroduced known deficiencies, the Confederation made excellent use of C3 and Raven tandems, bringing mobile 'Mech-mounted artillery to the forefront of combined-arms doctrine. The far superior O-Bakemono might not exist if not for the C3 paving the way for 'Mech-mounted artillery.

In the years surrounding the Clan Invasion, the Capellan Confederation and Draconis Combine retained the largest active Catapult formations, though numerous Periphery realms continued to field centuries-old examples. Variant development continued through the FedCom Civil War, the Jihad, and into the Dark Age, with both Hollis Incorporated on Corey and Yori 'Mech Works on Al Na'ir and later Algedi producing new models. The Catapult's proven adaptability across fire-support, direct-fire, and artillery roles has cemented its legacy as one of the Inner Sphere's most enduring heavy BattleMech platforms.
BMCatapult_CPLTC1.deployment: The base CPLT-C1 was the original Catapult configuration produced by Hollis Incorporated beginning in 2561. Produced in record numbers during the initial three-year Terran Hegemony contract, the C1 served extensively with Star League Defense Force second-line formations and remained the most commonly encountered variant throughout the Succession Wars era. Commanders who fielded the C1 learned to position it near supply lines to offset its limited ammunition endurance, and the variant's long service life produced a deep institutional knowledge base that informed the development of nearly every subsequent Catapult configuration.

The twin PPCs were upgraded to Extended Range models, and the machine guns were replaced with paired ER medium lasers for more effective close-range defense. Twenty double heat sinks managed the increased thermal demands, while thirteen and a half tons of armor provided excellent protection for a 'Mech of its weight class. The K2K represented a thorough modernization of the Kurita direct-fire doctrine, transforming the Catapult into a fast, well-protected energy weapons platform.

BMClint_CLNT23T.overview:
The Clint was commissioned in 2607 by the Star League Defense Force from Andoran Industries Limited, a minor BattleMech firm on Bell that secured the contract under the Star League Armaments Act by undercutting competitors with cost-cutting design features. Mass production of the CLNT-2-3T began in 2608, with over 300 units built before the fall of the Star League and the destruction of Andoran's factories during fighting between House Davion and House Liao.

Designed primarily as an inexpensive reconnaissance unit with the capabilities of a well-armed, low-end medium 'Mech, the Clint fulfilled its intended role admirably despite significant maintenance challenges. The design's non-standard components and shoddy construction made it a technician's nightmare, but its combination of speed, firepower, and an exceptional targeting system ensured its continued service across the Inner Sphere and Periphery for centuries.
BMClint_CLNT23T.capabilities:
The original Clint prototypes mounted a heavier Armstrong Buster-class autocannon, but chassis stress problems during testing forced Andoran to downgrade to the lighter Armstrong J11 autocannon/5. This weapon provides reliable medium-range firepower, complemented by a pair of Martell medium lasers that give the Clint effective close-range punch. The design's limited ammunition supply can force pilots to rely entirely on their lasers during prolonged engagements.

The Clint's Pitban 240 fusion engine propels the 'Mech to speeds approaching 100 kilometers per hour, while Andoran Model JJII jump jets provide 180 meters of jumping capability, allowing it to keep pace with other reconnaissance elements and maneuver effectively through broken terrain. This mobility, combined with the exceptional Sloane 220 Lockover targeting system, compensates significantly for the design's maintenance difficulties.

The Clint exemplifies the adage that one's ride was built by the lowest bidder. Its non-standard components require specific replacements that cannot be easily exchanged with other BattleMech types, and parts rarely lasted a year under normal use. The gyroscope became particularly notorious, with replacement units commanding prices literally worth their weight in gold during the Succession Wars. Despite these flaws, engineers who can look past the poor-quality parts generally agree that the overall design is steady and reliable.
BMClint_CLNT23T.history:
The destruction of Andoran Industries during the First Succession War was comprehensive, eliminating not only the original Clint blueprints but also all records of production numbers and official variants. Houses Davion and Liao took possession of the lion's share of surviving Clints, shipping most to remote locations for garrison duty, though the Capellans maintained several in front-line units. The design proved popular in the Periphery, and Clints could be found throughout the Inner Sphere, though the origins of many machines and whether their differing loadouts represented factory variants or field refits remained unknown.

During the First Succession War, Davion and Liao forces clashed on Bell, with bombing attacks reducing the planet's cities to rubble. House Liao deployed ten Clints in urban centers where they proved their worth. Liao subsequently sent several to the Marik front, where they participated in battles on Pella and Ingersoll against the Free Worlds League's Protectorate Guard. The Arcturan Guard of House Steiner acquired a Clint during a raid on Alula Australis, using it effectively in urban combat on Alexandria and Ryde.

An estimated 200 Clints remained in service through the Clan Invasion, mostly with Capellan forces or scattered along the Federated Suns' border regions. The Capellan Confederation introduced the 2-3U upgrade variant, which was subsequently adopted by the Federated Commonwealth after Bell Refit Yards established operations on the ruins of the original Andoran complex. Using all-new tooling painstakingly reverse-engineered by Defiance Industries from captured examples, the design's blueprints eventually reached Defiance's Furillo facility, which began producing new Clints in 3055 following repeated CCAF raids on Bell.

The FedCom Civil War and Jihad prompted further development, with Defiance releasing the 5U model during the Civil War and the 6S following the fall of Hesperus II to Blakist forces. Word of Blake assistance enabled the Taurian Concordat to establish Clint production at Pinard Protectorates Limited on MacLeod's Land, introducing the 3-3T variant. Production continued into the ilClan era with the 3-4T, a sensible upgrade that shares components with the Cadaver and finally addresses many of the design's troublesome non-standard features.
BMClint_CLNT23T.deployment: The standard production model introduced in 2608, the 2-3T addressed the prototype's chassis stress problems by downgrading the primary weapon to an Armstrong J11 AC/5 while adding a second medium laser and Andoran Model JJII jump jets. This configuration proved well-balanced for its intended reconnaissance role, combining acceptable firepower with excellent mobility. The 2-3T formed the basis for all subsequent Inner Sphere Clint variants and remained the most common configuration throughout the Succession Wars, found in service with nearly every major military force and numerous mercenary commands.

BMCommando_COM2D.overview:
First tested in 2463 by the Coventry Defense Conglomerate, the Commando is a twenty-five ton light BattleMech designed for reconnaissance and raiding. One of the Lyran Commonwealth's earliest homegrown designs, the primitive COM-1A gave way to the definitive COM-2D in 2486, transforming the Commando into a deadly close-range striker that has remained in continuous production for over six centuries.

Manufactured primarily by Coventry Metal Works, the Commando earned a fearsome reputation as a fast, hard-hitting scout capable of punching well above its weight class when deployed in groups. Its widespread production and countless field variants have made it one of the most recognizable light 'Mechs in the Inner Sphere.
BMCommando_COM2D.capabilities:
The standard COM-2D Commando mounts paired short-range missile launchers providing ten tubes of firepower, complemented by an arm-mounted medium laser. This armament allows the twenty-five ton 'Mech to deliver devastating barrages effective against even assault-class machines when deployed in groups. The dual missile system prevents a single lucky hit from disabling all offensive capability, and pilots can concentrate fire on one target or split between two.

This firepower comes at significant cost. Each launcher draws from its own ammunition bin and cannot share reserves, meaning the Commando often exhausts its missiles within minutes of sustained combat. The four tons of armor equals that of lighter scouts, creating fatal vulnerability against heavier opponents. Without jump jets, the design struggles to disengage in rough terrain and cannot escape determined pursuit by larger 'Mechs.

The Commando excels in hit-and-run strikes, scouting in pairs to pin down enemy reconnaissance units, and rapid flanking maneuvers. Against the Draconis Combine's Panther, however, that heavier machine's superior range and jump capability proved an effective counter to Commando hunter-killer groups.
BMCommando_COM2D.history:
The Commando's development was driven by desperation. After Operation Prometheus gave the Lyran Commonwealth stolen Terran Hegemony BattleMech technology in 2455, Kurita raiders struck Coventry in 2461 and secured enough data to jumpstart the Combine's own program. The following year, disgruntled Alarion workers defected to the Free Worlds League with additional plans. Knowing its enemies would soon field their own 'Mechs, the Commonwealth rushed the COM-1A into service in 2463, followed by the definitive COM-2D in 2486 after the original's cooling problems proved insurmountable.

The Commando became a cornerstone of Lyran reconnaissance forces and remained exclusively Commonwealth property for centuries. The Star League attempted repeatedly to acquire the design, but Lyran officials employed clever stalling and subtle deception to keep it from foreign hands. This changed during the Amaris Civil War when Lyran volunteers, disaffected by their government's neutrality, brought Commandos into Star League service with the Loyalist forces that liberated Terra. Some of these 'Mechs accompanied General Kerensky into exile, eventually becoming the basis for the Clan Commando IIC.

The Succession Wars spread the Commando throughout the Inner Sphere as mercenary units acquired examples and developed numerous field modifications. These "dash-seven" variants emerged from refit bays across known space, with Mech-it-Lube franchises becoming particularly associated with Commando modifications. The creation of the Federated Commonwealth finally broke the Lyran monopoly, making the Commando the standard light 'Mech alongside the Valkyrie. Vandenberg Mechanized Industries received license to produce the COM-2D for the Taurian Defense Force, while the Marian Hegemony developed its own rocket-armed COM-4H variant.

Task Force Serpent's campaign against Huntress in 3060 saw extensive use of upgraded dash-seven variants, prompting Coventry Metal Works to dedicate factory space for official recreations of these successful field modifications. The Word of Blake's occupation of Coventry from 3068 to 3074 resulted in the COM-7B variant optimized for hunting Lyran resistance fighters, including the Bradford family forces that continued to defy Blakist rule. The technological recovery of the thirty-first and thirty-second centuries brought further refinements, including the C3-equipped COM-8S spotter and the paradigm-shifting COM-9S long-range harasser.
BMCommando_COM2D.deployment: Introduced in 2486, this variant represents the definitive Commando configuration that established the design's reputation as a deadly striker. Six centuries of continuous production have made the 2D the most numerous variant, serving as the baseline from which countless modifications have emerged. Lyran reconnaissance lances relied on the 2D as their standard light 'Mech for generations, and licensed production for the Taurian Defense Force through Vandenberg Mechanized Industries ensured the variant's presence across the Periphery as well.

BMCyclops_CP10Z.overview:
The Cyclops began production in 2710 at Stormvanger Assemblies, Unlimited on Caph as an assault-weight command platform for Star League Defense Force field officers. Designed to combine the firepower expected of a ninety-ton 'Mech with sophisticated command-and-control electronics, the Cyclops filled a critical niche as a mobile headquarters capable of directing brigade-scale operations from the cockpit. The centerpiece of the design is its Tacticon B-2000 Battle Computer, a holographic battle management system that, when paired with the Olmstead 840 communications suite, grants planetary-scale coordination capability.

The destruction of Stormvanger's Caph facility during the Amaris Civil War in 2774 ended original production, and centuries of attrition without replacement parts left fewer than ten percent of surviving Cyclops frames with functional B-2000 systems by the late Succession Wars. Grumium Creations eventually restarted production on Grumium for the Free Rasalhague Republic, Com Guards, and Draconis Combine, breathing new life into the venerable command chassis with modernized variants.
BMCyclops_CP10Z.capabilities:
Powered by a Hermes 360 fusion engine, the Cyclops achieves a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, making it one of the faster assault 'Mechs in service. This mobility serves its command role well, allowing rapid repositioning as tactical situations evolve. Ten tons of Starshield Special armor provide adequate protection for a 'Mech intended to operate behind the front lines with a headquarters lance escort, though this falls well short of the protection expected of dedicated assault platforms. The distinctive single viewport of the cockpit, while providing excellent pilot visibility, leaves the head section and its irreplaceable electronics vulnerable to headhunting attacks.

The standard armament reflects a generalist philosophy. A Zeus-36 Mark III Autocannon/20 dominates close-range engagements, backed by a Hovertec Quad SRM-4 and twin Diverse Optics Type 20 medium lasers. A Delta Dart LRM-10 provides indirect fire capability, giving the design coverage across all range brackets. This diverse loadout ensures the Cyclops can defend itself in any situation, though ammunition dependency across multiple weapon systems limits sustained combat endurance.

The true value of the Cyclops lies in its electronics suite. The Tacticon B-2000 holographic battle computer allows a single MechWarrior to coordinate formations up to brigade strength, while the Olmstead 840 tight beam communications system with SatNav module enables planet-wide and surface-to-orbit communications. When operating with ample support from a headquarters lance and higher-echelon command apparatus, the Cyclops's shortcomings in armor and firepower become far less consequential, and the 'Mech can be held in reserve to turn the tide of battle or exploit an enemy weakness.
BMCyclops_CP10Z.history:
Stormvanger Assemblies, Unlimited delivered the first Cyclops from its Caph production lines in 2710, fulfilling a Star League Defense Force requirement for an assault-weight mobile command platform. SLDF tactical doctrine placed the Cyclops in reserve positions, guarded by headquarters lances and supporting elements, where its B-2000 battle computer could coordinate regimental and brigade-scale operations without exposing the design's relatively thin armor to direct assault. The CP-10-HQ variant followed in 2753, mounting a Collapsible Command Vehicle Module that extended the Cyclops's headquarters capabilities beyond the cockpit. Though the 'Mech earned an unfair reputation among officers who attempted to employ it as a frontline assault platform comparable to the more heavily armored Awesome or Stalker, those who used the Cyclops in its intended command role found it an unparalleled asset.

The Amaris Civil War proved catastrophic for the design when Rim Worlds Republic forces destroyed Stormvanger's Caph factory in 2774, permanently ending original production. Through the Succession Wars, spare parts for the sophisticated B-2000 computer became increasingly scarce. By the end of the era, only an estimated ten percent of surviving Cyclops frames retained functional battle computers. Stripped of their defining electronic systems, these 'Mechs were pressed into conventional assault service as bodyguards or decoys for actual commanding officers. Many pilots experimented with false head protectors to guard the vulnerable cockpit, a practice the NAIS eventually found counterproductive after the Fourth Succession War, as the modifications restricted vision and created additional shrapnel hazards during weapons impacts. The CP-10-Q field refit, which replaced the autocannon with additional LRM capacity and armor, emerged as one attempt to adapt the de-fanged Cyclops to a more survivable fire support role.

The discovery of the Helm Memory Core ignited attempts to replicate the B-2000, but these efforts bore no fruit before the Clan Invasion. The simultaneous development of the C3 computer network and doctrinal shifts toward using DropShips as mobile command posts further diminished enthusiasm for the Cyclops's dedicated command role. The CP-11-A field modification, replacing the autocannon with a Zeus Slingshot Gauss rifle, became the most common upgrade during this period. However, where a Cyclops with a functional B-2000 participated in operations, its effects on the outcome remained noticeable, ensuring the design retained its prestige among high-ranking officers.

Grumium Creations, a small military parts manufacturer on Grumium that ComStar had upgraded to serve both the Com Guards and the KungsArmé following the loss of Terra, proved instrumental in reviving the design. The company secured contracts to produce fully modernized Cyclops variants, beginning with the CP-11-G for the Second Star League Defense Force, Com Guards, and Free Rasalhague Republic in 3058, followed by the DCMS-oriented CP-12-K in 3059. These new-build frames reestablished the Cyclops as a viable frontline command platform with contemporary technology.

The Jihad proved a turbulent period for Cyclops production. Grumium Creations continued to operate under Clan Ghost Bear occupation following the formation of the Ghost Bear Dominion, though production operated at only sixty percent capacity by 3079. A Manei Domini Shadow Division assault on the Grumium compound in 3080 caused further disruption. Meanwhile, factory-level refits of older Cyclops frames were carried out at Hollis Incorporated on Corey and Lexatech Industries on Hun Ho, producing the dual-Gauss CP-11-B. The proliferation of electronic countermeasures on Jihad-era battlefields also spurred development of the CP-11-C2 and CP-11-C3 C3 networking variants. Following the Jihad, Grumium Creations struggled to attract funding for production line upgrades and shuttered its Crockett line, though Cyclops and Viking production continued. The Cyclops C, a Clan-tech garrison variant featuring hardened armor and Clan-grade weaponry, eventually emerged from the Grumium lines during the Dark Age for Rasalhague Dominion garrison Clusters, with surplus units offered on the open market.
BMCyclops_CP10Z.deployment: This variant represents the original Cyclops configuration as produced for the SLDF beginning in 2710. Its combination of the Zeus-36 Mark III Autocannon/20, Delta Dart LRM-10, Hovertec Quad SRM-4, and twin Diverse Optics medium lasers provides coverage across all engagement ranges. The Tacticon B-2000 battle computer and Olmstead 840 communications suite form the heart of the design, enabling brigade-level command from the cockpit. Though production ceased with the destruction of Stormvanger's Caph facility in 2774, surviving CP-10-Z frames remain in service across the Inner Sphere, with those retaining functional B-2000 systems among the most prized command platforms in any military inventory.

BMDervish_DV6M.overview:
The Dervish was designed in 2520 by Coventry Defense Conglomerate as a simple, missile-armed fire support 'Mech for the Lyran Commonwealth militia market. Originally built with exclusively ballistic and missile armament to ease maintenance for militia technicians, the design gained immediate acceptance and was soon licensed to manufacturers across the Inner Sphere. The Terran Hegemony later funded a comprehensive modernization to the DV-6M standard in 2610, cementing the chassis as a staple of the Star League Defense Force.

A 55-ton medium design, the Dervish earned a reputation as a mobile fire support platform, sometimes dismissed as a "poor man's Archer," though its pilots strongly dispute this characterization. Achernar BattleMechs on New Avalon became the primary manufacturer through the Succession Wars, and the design has remained in continuous production for over six centuries, making it one of the most enduring BattleMech designs in service.
BMDervish_DV6M.capabilities:
The Dervish relies on mobility and long-range firepower to accomplish its fire support mission. Twin Federated 10-Shot LRM-10 launchers, deeply embedded in the 'Mech's torso for protection, provide effective ranged fire support comparable to heavier designs. Supporting Federated 2-Shot SRM launchers are self-contained within the paddle-like forearms, originally serving as the only auxiliary weapons before designers added a ChisComp 39 medium laser atop each launcher to reduce ammunition dependency. Five Swingline X-100 jump jets (originally an afterthought in the design) have proven invaluable, granting 150 meters of jumping capability that allows the Dervish to exploit terrain, close with opponents, or extract from difficult engagements.

The design's primary weaknesses lie in its armor protection and lack of hand actuators. Seven and a half tons of Maximillian 105 armor provides adequate protection against light and medium weapons but proves insufficient against concentrated heavy firepower. The absence of hands limits the 'Mech's utility outside combat and restricts close-quarters fighting capability. Commanders face an uncomfortable tradeoff between adding armor and sacrificing the very firepower that defines the Dervish's role. Despite these limitations, the chassis is renowned for being easy to maintain and durable in extended campaigns, qualities that have kept it in frontline and garrison service across centuries of warfare.
BMDervish_DV6M.history:
The Dervish's origins trace to 2520 when Coventry Defense Conglomerate recognized a growing demand for simple, easy-to-maintain BattleMechs among Lyran Commonwealth militia units. The original DV-1S proved so successful that when unauthorized copies appeared in the Draconis Combine, Coventry chose to license production to manufacturers throughout the Inner Sphere during the mid-2500s. By the dawn of the Star League, First Lord Ian Cameron directed Coventry to revisit the design using modern technologies, and thousands of League-subsidized refits brought existing Dervishes up to the improved DV-6M standard during the years leading to the Reunification War.

Service in the Star League Defense Force ensured the Dervish's widespread proliferation, with examples eventually turning up as far as the Deep Periphery among the forces of Nueva Castile. The most celebrated engagement involving the chassis occurred on 23 March 2789 during the First Succession War, when elements of the Tenth Robinson Chevaliers (their "Whirling Dervishes") conducted a guerrilla campaign on New Rhodes III against Kurita's Second Sword of Light. Operating from the thick forests surrounding the planet's capital, a force of Dervishes and Enforcers destroyed supply dumps with repeated hit-and-fade attacks, significantly disrupting the Kurita drive toward New Avalon. The resulting boost to morale on both New Rhodes III and New Avalon, where smuggled tapes of the attacks were broadcast, cemented the Dervish's legendary status.

Over the course of the Succession Wars, attrition and parts shortages reduced the Dervish's numbers, and all but one of Achernar's factories was destroyed. The Federated Suns maintained the sole remaining production line, making the 'Mech particularly popular with the Avalon Hussars and earmarking it for newly forming Federated Commonwealth regiments after the Fourth Succession War. The DV-7D upgrade of 3047 incorporated recovered Star League technology, boosting sales, though Achernar was forced to lobby House Davion heavily to maintain orders. Ironically, the run-up to the FedCom Civil War and the conflict itself generated enough demand to keep the production lines running.

In the civil war's aftermath, the Federated Suns continued purchasing upgraded Dervishes while the Lyran Alliance shifted to the Griffin. Older models found homes in militia and reserve units across the Inner Sphere, while smaller mercenary outfits valued the 'Mech for its durability and ease of maintenance. During the Jihad, the disruption of supply lines prompted a revival of retrotech manufacturing, with companies such as Sword of the Prophet Enterprises on Algedi producing primitive DV-1S models for militia forces desperate for any available BattleMechs.

The fall of New Avalon in 3146 interrupted development of the latest Dervish variant, but the Draconis Combine seized the opportunity, reverse-engineering Achernar's captured work over three years to produce the DV-11DK, the first Combine-built Dervish variant. Pairing Combine-manufactured ClanTech missile launchers with captured Davion laser technology, the 11DK represents the latest chapter in the Dervish's remarkable six-century service history.
BMDervish_DV6M.deployment: The definitive production standard of the Dervish, this variant represented a comprehensive modernization funded by the Terran Hegemony beginning in 2610. The upgrade added twin ChisComp 39 medium lasers atop the forearm SRM launchers to reduce ammunition dependency, replaced the primitive engine and cockpit with modern equivalents, and increased maximum speed to 86 kph while extending jump capacity to 150 meters. The additional firepower and improved performance made this variant the backbone of fire support lances across the Inner Sphere for centuries, with Achernar BattleMechs on New Avalon eventually maintaining the most enduring production line through the Succession Wars.
