BMWhitworth_WTH1.overview:
The Whitworth was first manufactured in 2610 as a medium BattleMech intended to fill the weight gap between the lighter Wasp and heavier Phoenix Hawk designs. Originally conceived as a missile support platform for scout and strike lances, the Whitworth emerged from the Whitworth Company's design bureau on Dieron as a competent if unremarkable machine. Known colloquially as the "Tin Woodsman" among both critics and admirers, the design offered respectable firepower and adequate armor protection for its intended fire support role.

Despite an enduring reputation for mechanical unreliability in its lower actuator systems, the Whitworth proved serviceable enough to see widespread deployment across the Star League and its successor states, earning a place as a rugged if ungainly workhorse in armies throughout the Inner Sphere.
BMWhitworth_WTH1.capabilities:
The Whitworth's primary armament consists of two Longbow-10 LRM launchers mounted in the torsos, providing substantial long-range firepower for a medium 'Mech. These weapons are slaved to the Garret D2J targeting system (the same anti-aircraft tracking system employed by the Rifleman and Quickdraw) giving respectable accuracy against aerial and ground targets alike. Three Intek medium lasers provide adequate close-range defense when enemies close the distance.

The design's most significant limitation is its slow maximum speed of 64 km/h, over 30 km/h slower than the Wasps and Phoenix Hawks it was designed to support. Four Whitworth Jetlift jump jets split between the legs partially compensate for this deficiency. Eight tons of Durallex Light armor provide reasonable protection, distributed heavily around the legs to protect the design's notorious weak point, a faulty actuator system in the hips and legs that can cause limbs to tear loose during aggressive maneuvering. Houses have been known to replace failed legs with those salvaged from other 'Mech designs, creating bizarre but functional hybrids.
BMWhitworth_WTH1.history:
The Whitworth's origins trace to the Reunification War era, when the Whitworth Company on Dieron sought to create a medium fire support platform for Star League forces. The original WTH-1S model carried Harpoon-6 SRM launchers that encouraged pilots to engage in close-range combat for which the design was poorly suited, resulting in heavy losses. By 2689, Star League defense planners mandated the replacement of these weapons with Longbow-10 LRM launchers, creating the WTH-1 that would become the standard production model.

During the Star League era, the Whitworth served in both SLDF scout units and mobile strike lances, often deployed alongside Wolverines and Phoenix Hawks for reconnaissance-in-force missions, or providing fire support to heavier formations of Riflemen and Warhammers. The Rim Worlds Republic also fielded Whitworths, including the infamous WTH-0 variant used to devastating effect during the Amaris Civil War, where Republic forces employed inferno missiles and flamers to raze entire cities.

The destruction of the Whitworth Company's Dieron facility in 2776 during the Amaris Crisis eliminated the primary source of spare parts, condemning surviving Whitworths to gradual attrition throughout the Succession Wars. By the end of this era, fewer than three hundred remained operational, mostly in the hands of MechWarrior families who had passed the machines down through generations. The design earned the unflattering nickname "Worthless" among Federated Suns and Draconis Combine pilots, though the 'Mechs themselves continued to serve their units well.

The situation changed in 3035 when Whitworth Specialty Manufacturing was incorporated on Benjamin, reportedly with ComStar assistance as part of aid offered to Theodore Kurita. This company began producing spare parts and later developed upgrade kits following the Clan Invasion. Despite these efforts, most Whitworths were decommissioned from Great House militaries by the mid-3050s, finding new homes among mercenary companies and Periphery nations like the Taurian Concordat and Outworlds Alliance.

The Jihad prompted renewed interest in the platform, with both the Federated Suns and Draconis Combine developing C3-equipped variants to counter Blakist improved C3 technology. More recently, Marian Arms Inc. on Alphard has begun producing an improved variant that has spread throughout the Inner Sphere via salvage and Draconis Combine contracts, ensuring the Whitworth's continued presence on battlefields across known space.
BMWhitworth_WTH1.deployment: The standard production model that became synonymous with the Whitworth name, this variant replaced the original SRM armament with Longbow-10 LRM launchers following Star League mandate in 2689. This configuration transformed the design from a flawed close-range brawler into a competent fire support platform, though its slow speed continued to hamper its effectiveness in the reconnaissance role for which it was nominally designed. The WTH-1 served with distinction throughout the Star League era and Succession Wars, becoming the most common variant encountered across the Inner Sphere.

BMZeus_ZEU6S.overview: The Zeus is an eighty-ton assault BattleMech first built by Defiance Industries on Hesperus II for the Lyran Commonwealth in 2787, just as the First Succession War began. Built at the request of Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces commanders for a new light-assault 'Mech designed to engage the enemy at long range and perform hit-and-run attacks, the Zeus filled a critical gap in the Lyran arsenal. The design quickly became the pride of the LCAF, serving as the quintessential Lyran assault platform for over three centuries. Defiance Industries' exclusive production at Hesperus II ensured a steady supply, though it also made the design's availability dependent on the security of that single vital world. The Zeus earned a reputation for rugged dependability and versatile combat performance that few assault designs of any era have matched.
BMZeus_ZEU6S.capabilities:
The Zeus is fast enough to keep up with most heavy 'Mechs, and with a sturdy frame, eleven and a half tons of standard armor and a versatile weapons array, is equally capable of defeating them. Its use of reliable, low-maintenance and easily modified systems at a time when most 'Mechs were built with cutting-edge technology also proved fortuitous, allowing the Zeus to be produced long after those advanced components had become Lostech.

The standard Zeus carries a mix of ballistic, missile, and energy weapons covering all engagement ranges. A primary weapon in the left arm provides long-range striking power, backed by a missile launcher in the right arm for sustained indirect or direct fire support. A large laser in the left torso handles intermediate engagements, while paired medium lasers address close-range threats and rear-arc defense. This combination ensures the Zeus remains dangerous at any distance, though pilots must manage heat carefully during sustained engagements. The design's eighty-ton chassis achieves a maximum speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, unusually fast for an assault platform and a deliberate choice by Defiance's engineers to support the hit-and-run doctrine Lyran commanders envisioned.
BMZeus_ZEU6S.history:
Three years before its release, the first two prototypes of the Zeus would have their first "test run" when they were forced to repel an attack on the Hesperus II factory by the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. As the enemy pushed through Lyran lines, the two 'Mechs were summoned to aid, and through sheer novelty and long-range firepower, the Kuritans were forced to pause. This enabled more reinforcements to push back DCMS forces. While these prototypes were effective in repelling the attack, they were considerably more advanced than the commercial model and armed with a PPC, which proved unpredictable and unreliable during the combat. Inadequate shielding caused wild magnetic interactions between the weapon and the Zeus' engine, which was later revealed to be the source of this behavior. To guarantee that the Zeus arrived at the front lines as soon as possible, the complex energy weapon was replaced with a basic autocannon. The 'Mech initially appeared in substantial numbers after the 15th Lyran Guards regained the planet Sakhalin, and the Zeus had a long and storied history within the Commonwealth during the Succession Wars, becoming a well-respected assault 'Mech. Engineers were able to put a PPC on the Zeus again after the end of the Third Succession War, with the resulting ZEU-6T variant being the standard during the Fourth Succession War and later the War of 3039. The design was also well received by mercenary units, particularly the Zeta Battalion of Wolf's Dragoons.

During the formation of the Federated Commonwealth, the Zeus would meet opposition from some former AFFS troops, whose "Davion pride" barred them from using the 'Mech despite its superiority to many of their own machines. Similarly, as the FedCom military began to take on a Davion character, many Lyran commanders insisted that their pride and joy was too vital to give up, and so urged Defiance Industries to build new models that included freshly recovered Star League Lostech. With the introduction of the ZEU-9S Zeus, production of the earlier variations would be halted, and samples of this hallmark Lyran 'Mech would be distributed throughout the Commonwealth as a symbol of the new partnership. However, at the time of the FedCom Civil War, the majority of Zeus 'Mechs were in Lyran hands, with many of those assigned to Davion units relegated to rear-guard duty or sold to mercenaries. The LAAF and, following their takeover of Hesperus II in 3070, the Word of Blake Militia would continue to receive new variations.
BMZeus_ZEU6S.deployment: This variant mounted a Defiance Type J Autocannon/5 in the left arm as its primary weapon, backed up by a Coventry Star Fire LRM-15 in the right arm for engaging enemies at long ranges. The missile launcher's placement, set around and back from a central core, was a unique way to protect the weapon while allowing the Zeus to use that arm as a bludgeon in hand-to-hand combat; the complicated arrangement also made the launcher prone to failure without regular maintenance. Both were fed by a ton of ammunition each, a source of concern among some pilots who preferred more shots from the LRM-15, though others noted by the point it ran dry the armor was probably compromised and an empty missile bin was less likely to explode. The Thunderbolt A5M Large Laser, mounted in the left torso and used to engage enemies at intermediate ranges, was also a unique challenge for Defiance. Whereas a typical barrel-type large laser wouldn't fit in the compact space, the company used their rare knowledge of fiber optics to design a smaller though no less effective weapon. Finally two Defiance B3M medium lasers, one mounted in the center torso and one in the left facing rearwards, were used for close-in work. This combination of weaponry made the Zeus a 'Mech that was deadly at any range.
